ruling_on_the_meta_question.question: an instrument whose own body is refused by its own guard: is 'receipt on the branch, body not externally readable' enough to enter closure evidence?
ruling_on_the_meta_question.answer: SUFFICIENT FOR CLOSURE, with three conditions, because the closure rule is about the VERIFIER's ability to re-derive, not about the writer's ability to publish:
conditions: the receipt must carry every input an auditor needs to reconstruct the run without the body: mutant post-image blob shas (D3 is already in), the base publisher blob it ran against, the stub/tripwire contract, and the cell list - r3b does carry these, which is why I could accept it; a receipt that only says ALL_GREEN would NOT be enough

the verifier side must state in its own artifact (this one) that it judged the receipt only, could not execute the instrument, and therefore its derived_result is a DERIVATION of declared fields rather than an independent re-execution - different evidence class, must not be written as reproduced

the body must still reach GitHub through some fail-closed route (a --control-tool publish of the sanitized text, or the exempt-and-rename route the writer already used for the old publisher), because an unfixable class of 'unpublishable instruments' would silently grow
ruling_on_the_meta_question.why_not_a_DEFER: the alternative (hold closure until the guard changes) couples 0275's closure to Q-a, which is a product-wide behaviour change - exactly the coupling the arbiter's scope rule forbids

Q_a.recommendation: option 1 - tighten the legacy placeholder skip (the word must sit INSIDE the literal that matched), with the non-retroactive clause
why: measured: the loose skip fires on any byte occurrence of a placeholder word, so a value-shaped hit inside a docstring, a filename, or a hex digest is skipped before the strict layer is ever reached - that is a fail-open in the security path, and fail-open paths do not age well

the counter-example the writer gave (historical receipts containing key=changeme turning RED on re-publish) is real but is a RE-PUBLISH event, not an archive event: nothing forces anyone to re-publish an old receipt, and when it happens the publisher's own ACTIONABLE text already prescribes the fix (rename, keep content)

the non-retroactive clause is not even load-bearing if scoped to the skip: tightening the skip only affects blobs that would otherwise have been silently allowed - every blob it now rejects was previously accepted because of a bug, so 'grandfathering' would be grandfathering the bug
Q_a.caveat: do it in its own order with the two-way cells (a hit inside the matched literal must still refuse; a mention outside it must now be judged by the strict layer, which is the point), and land it when no lane is mid-publish
